analysis.title: Cemex SAB (CX): 3Q26 Model Update: An Attractive Entry Point; Reiterate Buy
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on Cemex (CX) after a third straight quarterly beat. 12-month price target cut from US$15.5 to US$15.0 (+50% return from the ~$10 level cited in the note, 38.5% upside vs the $10.83 close on 29 Oct 2026).

GS cites headwinds going into 2027: higher energy costs, upcoming cement capacity in Mexico and a weak US residential outlook. It expects Cemex to offset them through pricing, Mexican residential and infrastructure demand, and US infrastructure and industrial activity.

CX trades at 5x 2027E EV/EBITDA versus ~7x implied by the US$15.0 target, which GS says is in line with the stock's historical average. GS expects a 10% 2027E FCFE yield versus an approximately 1% dividend yield, which it says gives capacity for higher shareholder distributions.

Mexico drives the story: it accounts for 80% of this year's +22% EBITDA growth. Mexico's first-half EBITDA margin was approximately 37%, its strongest since 2021, and the expected 3Q26 margin moderation largely did not happen. GS expects overall EBITDA margin to rise ~100 bps to 22%, supporting 8% EBITDA growth for the year.
Management's conference-call tone was constructive. It views a 21% consolidated EBITDA margin as a floor, about 300 bps above the 2010-25 average.

Management expects energy costs to rise at a mid/high single digit rate. Half of total energy exposure is hedged (electricity, direct diesel, natural gas, alternative fuels), and pricing and efficiencies should offset more.

Management expects Mexican demand to stay resilient on government-backed housing and better infrastructure execution. US residential demand is unlikely to improve in 2027 but is not expected to deteriorate materially. Remaining IIJA funds and industrial investment support infrastructure demand and a flat cement volume outlook.

FY26 estimates are cut about 2% on management guidance for volumes and margins. 2026E EBITDA goes from US$3,738mn to US$3,657mn (-2%), 2027E from US$4,030mn to US$3,967mn, and 2028E from US$4,297mn to US$4,193mn. The 2027 outlook is described as unchanged.

Volume changes: 2026 Mexico ready mix is cut from 0.0% to -2.0% and Mexico aggregates from 3.0% to 0.0%. US ready mix goes from 0.0% to -1.0%, MEA aggregates from 3.0% to 0.0%, and SCAC aggregates from 1.9% to -20.0%. 4Q26 margin is also trimmed on higher maintenance and energy expense.

AMEA is the largest regional EBITDA cut: 2026E from US$317mn to US$279mn (-12%) and EBITDA margin from 19.4% to 17.2%. US 2026E EBITDA goes from US$981mn to US$918mn (-6%), with margin from 19.2% to 18.1%.

FX: GS FX forecasts MXN about 10% stronger than the forward curve (12-month forward 19.15 MXN per USD vs forecast 17.25). If current exchange rates hold, GS would expect a 4-5% hit to 2027 EBITDA, though at 5x+ 2027 EBITDA the valuation would still be attractive.

Comp sheet: CX at 5.2x 2027 EV/EBITDA, 7.1% 2027 FCFE yield and 9.7x 2026 P/E, versus US cement peers (Vulcan 14.2x, Amrize 7.6x, Titan America 6.4x EV/EBITDA 2027) and European peers (Holcim 8.8x, Heidelberg 6.1x).
GS price target for CEMEXCPO.MX is cut from MXN 26.7 to MXN 25.3, with the stock at P$20.47 (23.6% upside).

market_movers.rationale: Third consecutive quarterly beat, Mexico margin strength and a 10% 2027E FCFE yield support the Buy. The target is cut from $15.5 to $15 on lower FY26 volume and margin estimates.
The Mexican-listed CEMEXCPO.MX shares carry a Buy and a target cut from MXN 26.7 to MXN 25.3, on the same estimate changes as CX.
Comp sheet shows Holcim at Buy with a 88 target (29% return), a figure carried in the sector table rather than analyzed in the note.
Comp sheet shows Heidelberg Materials at Buy with a 210 target (43% return), carried in the sector table rather than analyzed in the note.
Comp sheet shows Buzzi S.p.A at Neutral with a 44 target (11% return), carried in the sector table rather than analyzed in the note.

earnings_insights: Cemex 3Q26 was another quarterly beat, the third in a row, per GS. The note gives no consensus figure for the beat.

3Q26 reported figures in GS's model: net sales US$4,590mn, operating EBITDA US$990mn, operating EBITDA margin 21.6% (reported actuals, not estimates). 4Q26 is a GS estimate: net sales US$4,256mn, EBITDA US$854mn, margin 20.1%.
3Q26 Mexico: net sales US$1,299mn, operating EBITDA US$480mn, margin 37.0% (reported). 3Q26 US: net sales US$1,373mn, EBITDA US$259mn, margin 18.9% (reported).

GS estimates for 2026E (all GS estimates): revenue US$17,459mn (+8% y/y), operating EBITDA US$3,657mn (+18% y/y), EBITDA margin 20.9%, majority net income US$1,473mn, EPS US$1.00 (old US$1.03). 2027E EPS US$1.07 (old US$1.10) and 2028E EPS US$1.22 (old US$1.27).
Quarterly EPS estimates from GS: US$0.28 for 9/26, US$0.34 for 12/26E, US$0.28 for 3/27E and US$0.33 for 6/27E. The 9/26 figure is not labeled as an estimate in the table.
Leverage in GS's model: net debt/operating EBITDA (IFRS16) of 1.2x for 2026E and 0.8x for 2027E, down to 0.4x in 2028E. The target-sheet table shows 0.9x, 0.5x and 0.2x for 12/26E to 12/28E.

Management guidance for 2026 volumes: cement low-single-digit increase (GS est +2.3%), ready mix low-single-digit decrease (GS est -0.1%) and aggregates low-single-digit decrease (GS est -1.2%) for Cemex overall.

trade_ideas.description: Long Cemex (CX) shares, Buy rating with a 12-month price target of US$15.0
trade_ideas.rationale: The stock trades at 5x 2027E EV/EBITDA versus ~7x implied by the target, with a 10% 2027E FCFE yield and room for higher shareholder distributions.
trade_ideas.risk: MXN depreciation, weaker pricing power across business lines, weaker residential markets in Mexico and the US, and costs of green initiatives in Europe.

risk_factors: MXN depreciation. At current exchange rates GS would expect a 4-5% hit to 2027 EBITDA.
Weakening pricing power across business lines.
Weaker residential markets in Mexico and the US.
Costs of green initiatives in Europe.
Higher energy costs, expected up at a mid/high single digit rate, with half of exposure hedged.
New cement capacity coming in Mexico.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 compares 2026 volume guidance with GS estimates: Cemex cement +2.3% (guidance low-single-digit increase), ready mix -0.1% and aggregates -1.2%. Mexico cement is +5.5% against guidance of low-to-mid single digit increase.
Exhibit 4 shows regional sales and EBITDA by quarter: Mexico 2026E EBITDA US$1,860mn (+33% y/y) and margin 36.0%, US 2026E EBITDA US$918mn (-6% y/y) and margin 18.1%.
Exhibit 6 comp sheet shows CX at 5.2x 2027 EV/EBITDA and 4.5x 2028 against a LatAm and global cement average of 4.8x and 4.0x (Mexico), and Europe cement average of 7.0x and 6.4x.
vol_and_positioning: Management notes investor interest in Cemex has increased and skews bullish, per GS.
GS M&A rank for Cemex is 3 (low, 0-15% probability of becoming an acquisition target), which GS treats as immaterial to the price target.

tension_points.bull_case: Mexico demand and margins are resilient (about 37% first-half margin), management treats a 21% consolidated margin as a floor, and pricing, hedging (half of energy exposure) and efficiencies offset higher energy costs.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy costs rise at a mid/high single digit rate, new cement capacity arrives in Mexico, US residential demand stays weak in 2027, and a stronger MXN would cut 2027 EBITDA by 4-5%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If current exchange rates are sustained rather than the peso strengthening to 17.25, GS would expect a 4-5% hit to 2027 EBITDA.
